- **Bounded reads in their statement** (`decision/bounded-readers`, `.claude/rules/security.md` 2026-11-16 addition): `take(reader, MAX_FRAME + 1).read_to_end(…)`; a read past `MAX_FRAME` is `config-oversize`.

- **Closed code words** (`viola_core::is_code_word`, `contract/code-word/format`) for every outcome word; no path, key or value in any line, stamp or summary (`decision/verify-lines-carry-no-content`).

capability: the 23rd relied ledger row `trust-record` in `viola-agent-claude`, probed by a SIXTH interactive
`viola verify` run (Run F) that writes the trust record for its own fresh OS-temp dir into the config file its child
reads, reads the child's first settled frame, and removes that one record of its own on every exit path the process
reaches (the founder's R4, relayed in `inputs#I1` item 3; arch `decision/capability-ledger-gate` · `decision/verify-child-set`).
The record writer is built ONCE, in a pure Claude half (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs`: the file the child
reads, the CLI's key, the record's form) and a root-bin I/O half (`src/trust_record.rs`: the file checks, the CLI's
lock when free, `viola_state::fs::replace_private` with the file's own mode, the read-back, at most 3 attempts), so
«Session folder trusted by viola» calls the same `src/trust_record.rs` from `run` / `revive` (R2, R3 as worded in
`inputs#I1` item 3; arch `decision/agent-claude-pure` · `decision/one-replace-helper`).

The probe can fail and its control can read the dialog: Run A (the untrusted twin, unchanged) must show the trust
modal, and Run F, identical but for the record, must settle on the input box with no modal; the fake agent decides
trust from a config file named on its argv (`--trust-config <file>`) under its OWN reading of the CLI's key rule, so a
writer that picks another file or another key leaves Run F on the modal and the row reads `fail` (`inputs#I1` item 4;
test-plan `decision/fake-agent-argv-only`). A file the writer cannot use — absent, unreadable, a link, not a regular
file, not the user's, oversize, not the JSON expected, an entry already at the key, the lock held three times, the
record lost three times — writes nothing and the row reads that closed word, never `pass`; when the CLI does NOT
honour a written record the row reads `fail`, the CLI version stays unverified for this row, and the product (next
entry) never writes: the dialog stays the human's (`decision/no-typing-into-trust-dialogs`).

Every test-started `viola verify` (the root stamping helpers and the harness boot) runs under a test-owned `HOME`
holding a seeded `.claude.json`, and hands the fake agent `--trust-config` for that file, so the tests' shared stamp
and CI stay green and no test writes the user's real `~/.claude.json` (scope, the P3 premise). One live
`viola verify` (S0) on the 2.1.325 install by path runs on the standing rig's new `V` arm under its private config,
with the spare S0-2 only to re-fire a start lost to its shape (`inputs#I1` item 6). Nothing of `viola run` or `revive`
changes; no capability is claimed.

1. **The record's pure half** — new `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs` (declared in `lib.rs`), no I/O:
   - `config_file(kept_config_dir: Option<&OsStr>, user_home: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PathBuf, TrustWord>`: the
     kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` value when the strip kept that name (an absolute, non-empty path → `<value>/.claude.json`;
     any other value → `config-dir-unusable`), else `<user home>/.claude.json` (no home → `home-unknown`). The caller
     passes the value only when `StripPlan::kept` holds `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; the read of that ONE value is R2's
     ratified read (`inputs#I1` item 3).
   - `record_key(canonical_cwd: &Path, git_root: Option<&Path>) -> String`: the git root inside a repository, else the
     canonical cwd — the key the CLI writes on an accepted dialog (scope §rootOnly reading).
   - `with_record(bytes, key) -> Result<Vec<u8>, TrustWord>`: parse (default depth) as a JSON object, `projects` absent
     or an object; an entry already at `key` → `key-present`; else insert `projects[key] = {"hasTrustDialogAccepted":
     true}` alone, every other key and entry kept; any other shape → `config-malformed`.
   - `without_record(bytes, key) -> Result<Vec<u8>, TrustWord>`: remove `projects[key]` whole (its key is verify's own
     fresh dir, so the whole entry is its own, whatever the CLI added to it); nothing else touched.
   - `holds_record(bytes, key) -> bool`: `projects[key].hasTrustDialogAccepted == true`.
   - `TrustWord`, the closed outcome words, each a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`): `written` · `removed` ·
     `config-absent` · `config-unreadable` · `config-link` · `config-not-regular` · `config-foreign` · `config-oversize`
     · `config-malformed` · `config-dir-unusable` · `home-unknown` · `key-present` · `lock-held` · `lost`.
   - The CLI's lock name as a literal beside the record's key names: `<file>.lock`, a directory (p3-block, the
     cancelled take-up's measurement, not re-derived).

2. **The writer, built once** — new `src/trust_record.rs` (declared in `src/main.rs`), the root bin, sync, no log line
   of its own (its outcome rides the caller's record):
   - `git_root(cwd)`: the nearest ancestor holding a `.git` entry that is a directory or a regular file, read through
     `symlink_metadata` (a link there is no root), none → `None`.
   - `write_record(file, key) -> TrustWord` and `remove_record(file, key) -> TrustWord`, each at most 3 attempts of:
     `symlink_metadata(file)` (absent → `config-absent`, a link → `config-link`, not a regular file →
     `config-not-regular`, owner not the effective user → `config-foreign`, all before any open); take the CLI's lock
     by creating `<file>.lock` as a 0700 directory — present → this attempt writes nothing, a fixed 100 ms pause, the
     next attempt (the third → `lock-held`); open with `O_NOFOLLOW`, read through `take(file, MAX_FRAME + 1)` (past
     `MAX_FRAME` → `config-oversize`, a read error → `config-unreadable`); transform (step 1); replace through
     `viola_state::fs::replace_private(file, bytes, <the file's own mode & 0o7777>)`; remove the lock dir it made, only
     that one; read back (bounded, the same way) — the record held (write) or gone (remove) → `written` / `removed`,
     else the next attempt (the third → `lost`). The lock is never removed unless this call created it; a failed
     replace leaves the file as it was (`replace_private`'s contract).
   - A test-only seam over the read-back window (a parameter of an inner function, like
     `viola_state::fs::place_private_new_with`; no env, flag or feature) lets a unit case rewrite the file between the
     replace and the read-back.

3. **The 23rd ledger row** — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`:
   - `LedgerRow::TrustRecord`, appended last to `ALL` (`[Self; 23]`), id `trust-record`, words `a trust record

     "pass"`), so every 22-row stamp reads unverified.

4. **Run F** — `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` `trust_record_run`, run LAST, after Run E (A–E keep their order and

   - A SIGKILLed verify (or a crash, or a failed handler install) leaves the one entry `projects[<its temp dir>] =

    <vhome> verify -- <program> <child args>` (`{cwd}` and a new `{config}` substituted), held until it exits or the
    stop; no key into anything (`keys: none`); after exit, read verify's exit code, `<vhome>/ledger/stamps.json`'s
    `rows.trust-record` for the probed version (`trust-record: <word>`) and its pass count, and — before the teardown
    — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` reads the private `.claude.json` for any `projects` key under the OS temp
    dir's `viola-verify-` prefix (`record-left: absent|present`, the bytes dropped). The summary also prints
    `stop:` beside `keys:` (the standing stop: Ctrl-C into its own pty, or a no-key group kill), `census`,
    `credentials`, `scratch` and the mark witness's `user-config`. Rehearsal over the fake agent in
    `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` (`rehearse v`, the fake given `--trusted-root {cwd} --trust-config
    {config}/.claude.json --screens --turn-stop --dialogs --framing --transcript`): `trust-record: pass`,
    `record-left: absent`.

14. **S0, live, by hand, once** — the round below: the 2.1.325 install read by path, the census, the build hash, S0
    ledgered with the clock's time before it is made; a start refused for the token window is uncounted (stop, say
    so, no timer); S0-2 only for a start lost to its shape. Its summary is the reading, whatever it reads.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs` — the record's pure half: the config file rule, the key rule, the transforms, the closed words
- `src/trust_record.rs` — the writer, built once for verify now and run / revive next
- `tests/contract_verify_home.rs` — the census that every test-started verify runs under a test-owned HOME
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod trust;`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — the 23rd row, `TypedRun`'s trust fields, its check arm, its stamp word and `measured.trust_probe`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases.rs` — `clean_typed()` and the row's cases
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_checks.rs` — the row's check cases
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` — the 22-id stamp unverified, the row word, `measured.trust_probe`
- `src/main.rs` — `mod trust_record;`
- `src/cmd/verify.rs` — the sixth run's inputs, the module doc, the `/23` unit cases
- `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` — six runs
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs` — Run F and its record guard
- `src/run/version_gate.rs` — its case literals
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — `--trust-config` and its own record read
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/test_cases_opts.rs` — the option's cases
- `tests/support/verify.rs` — the test-owned HOME, the seeded config, `--trust-config`
- `tests/support/home.rs` — the stamping path through those helpers
- `tests/cli_verify.rs` — the count literals and the trust cases
- `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` — its verify starts through the helpers, the stop table
- `tests/cli_verify/stamps.rs` — the older-stamp oracle, the stamped counts
- `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs` — the relied id list
- `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` — the new bounded reads
- `tests/channel_error_bodies.rs` — its stamping verify through the helpers
- `tests/cli_version_gate.rs` — its stamping verify through the helpers
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — boot step 4 under a session HOME with `--trust-config`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs` — the local-live row literals
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — the `V` arm
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` — the after-run record read, `{config}`
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — `v` and `S0` / `S0-2` in its usage text
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `v` rehearsal

The block runs the formatter and linter, the unit layers of the agent crate and the root bin (the writer, Run F's
pieces, the fake agent's option), the integration binaries this chunk changes by name, then the whole integration and
E2E layers (the stamping helpers and the harness boot reach every stamped binary), the release check (the fake agent
changed), the retired-count probe, then the live round for S0 and the operator pass. A change to the fake agent's
trust reading puts `cli_verify` in the block (verification-harness.md 2026-11-17). Every root test that waits keeps
the shared 12 s `WITHIN` bound under the 20 s lint; the verify-driven cases have no test-side bound, the `ci` 20 s kill
being theirs (test-plan `decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill`). No smoke entry: no boot-path of `viola run` changes
(the harness boot's stamping is exercised by the E2E layer). No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8).

The remove-the-guard controls are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, not entries (validation.md check 4 (6)),
each fired with `--timeout 900`, each control's entry the `cli_verify` integration entry below (it builds the workspace,
so the clone has the binaries; testing.md 2026-11-13), and «holds» means each named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT
line:

- `trust-nowrite` — `src/trust_record.rs`: `write_record`'s replace removed (the transformed bytes never written, the
  word still `written`); cases `verify_trust_record_row_passes_when_the_fake_reads_the_written_record`. With the guard
  gone the subject (verify) starts Run F on an unrecorded folder: the fake shows the trust form, the row reads `fail` —
  measured at implement by this control.

- `trust-noremove` — `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`: the `RecordGuard`'s `remove_record` call removed; cases
  `verify_trust_record_row_passes_when_the_fake_reads_the_written_record`,
  `verify_stopped_during_the_trust_record_run_removes_its_record_and_exits_1`. With the guard gone verify leaves its
  record in the config on every path — measured at implement by this control.

- `trust-cfgdir` — `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`: the kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` branch removed (the user home's file
  always); case `verify_trust_record_goes_to_the_kept_config_dir`. With the guard gone the record lands in the `HOME`
  file the child does not read and Run F shows the trust form — unmeasured until this control runs.
Each control's id is at most 16 characters; a `timeout` reading is not «holds» (it is the letter's to read).

  pause, at most 3) · the whole `projects[<own temp dir>]` entry is removed · the fake agent learns its config file by

  third fake-agent env seam», arch history 2026-10-16) · tests isolate by `HOME`, not by `claude_env_keep` (a kept

- `claude_env_keep` in the stamped test home — rejected: `copy_tree` copies it into every stamped home.

- A new verify refusal or process-exit code for the writer — rejected: a writer outcome is a row reading, not a
  refusal (`decision/verify-failing-row-no-refusal`).
- Creating an absent config file, or writing any key beside `hasTrustDialogAccepted` — rejected by R2.
- Removing a lock dir this call did not create, or a record another run wrote — rejected by R3 / R4.
- Touching `src/run/` or `src/cmd/revive.rs` — out of scope («Session folder trusted by viola»).

- Stamps going stale (`inputs#I1` item 5): once landed, `LedgerRow::relied()` holds 23 ids, so EVERY stamp of the 22
  older ids reads unverified to the new binary — the live home's 2.1.296 · .302 · .312 · .319 · .323 · .325 stamps

  its home stays as it is until that binary is rebuilt. A live home is re-stamped only by a live `viola verify` under
  the founder's cap, which this chunk does not take for the live home (S0 stamps the rig's scratch `vhome`, removed at
  teardown) — that re-stamp stays owed on «The 2.1.325 recorded fixture set». Until then, a rebuilt viola on the live
  home degrades to transport-only: `answer` exit 12, `/clear`, `/compact`, `/mcp` sends `unconfirmable` (layout

- A later live `viola verify` on a home that does NOT keep `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` writes its temp-dir record into the

1. **The record's pure half** — new `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/trust.rs` (declared in `lib.rs`), no I/O:
   - `config_file(kept_config_dir: Option<&OsStr>, user_home: Option<&Path>) -> Result<PathBuf, TrustWord>`: the
     kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` value when the strip kept that name (an absolute, non-empty path → `<value>/.claude.json`;
     any other value → `config-dir-unusable`), else `<user home>/.claude.json` (no home → `home-unknown`). The caller
     passes the value only when `StripPlan::kept` holds `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; the read of that ONE value is R2's
     ratified read (`inputs#I1` item 3).
   - `record_key(canonical_cwd: &Path, git_root: Option<&Path>) -> String`: the git root inside a repository, else the
     canonical cwd — the key the CLI writes on an accepted dialog (scope §rootOnly reading).
   - `with_record(bytes, key) -> Result<Vec<u8>, TrustWord>`: parse (default depth) as a JSON object, `projects` absent
     or an object; an entry already at `key` → `key-present`; else insert `projects[key] = {"hasTrustDialogAccepted":
     true}` alone, every other key and entry kept, in order (`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, `Cargo.toml:225`), the
     document written back pretty-printed with two-space indent (the CLI's own form; whitespace is not a key); any
     other shape → `config-malformed`.
   - `without_record(bytes, key) -> Result<Vec<u8>, TrustWord>`: remove `projects[key]` whole (its key is verify's own
     fresh dir, so the whole entry is its own, whatever the CLI added to it); nothing else touched.
   - `holds_record(bytes, key) -> bool`: `projects[key].hasTrustDialogAccepted == true`.
   - `TrustWord`, the closed outcome words, each a code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`): `written` · `removed` ·
     `config-absent` · `config-unreadable` · `config-link` · `config-not-regular` · `config-foreign` · `config-oversize`
     · `config-malformed` · `config-dir-unusable` · `home-unknown` · `key-present` · `lock-held` · `lost`.
   - The CLI's lock name as a literal beside the record's key names: `<file>.lock`, a directory (p3-block, the
     cancelled take-up's measurement, not re-derived).

10. **The trust cases** (root, `tests/cli_verify.rs` — verify-driven, the 20 s `ci` kill their bound, no test-side
    wait; new names):
    - `verify_trust_record_row_passes_when_the_fake_reads_the_written_record` — exit 0, `[23/23] trust-record …  pass`,
      `stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  0 fail`, the stamp's `rows.trust-record` `pass` and `measured.trust_probe` `{written,
      removed}`, and after verify the config holds no `projects` key under the OS temp dir's `viola-verify-` prefix,
      its seeded sentinel entry value-equal.
    - `verify_trust_record_row_fails_when_the_record_is_not_read` (the control) — the fake given `--trust-config` of
      ANOTHER file: Run F settles on the trust form, killed with no key, `[23/23] … fail`, `22 pass  1 fail`, exit 1,
      `rows.trust-record` `fail`, the record still removed.
    - `verify_trust_record_row_reads_config_absent_and_writes_nothing` — a `HOME` with no `.claude.json`: no file
      created, no Run F child (the fake receipt holds no start in a `viola-verify-` dir after Run E's), `rows.
      trust-record` `config-absent`, `… fail` on the step line.
    - `verify_trust_record_goes_to_the_kept_config_dir` — the home's `config.json` keeps `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the env

# Route adaptation relay — the split of «Session folder trusted by viola» (2026-11-17, from the Viola overseer)

First the take-up's cancel (this phase window), then a 0-pending `/andromeda-wrap-session` at HEAD `c2310c28`
(ci#44144048750 green 7 of 7). Three parts, per the operator scheme: the context, the items for disposition, the
anchors. The phase's P3 block of chunk `2026-11-17-session-folder-trusted-by-viola` is the measured ground
(`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T18-20-22Z-phase/p3-block.md`); nothing of it is re-derived here.

## 1. Context — the founder's own answers, given in the overseer's dialog and read at 2026-11-17T18:59:41Z (his option on each, verbatim labels)

- **R1 — the split: «Сначала строка реестра».** A NEW entry stands ahead of «Session folder trusted by viola»; the
  take-up of that entry is cancelled and it is taken up again second. The new entry holds the 23rd relied
  capability-ledger row (the CLI honours a trust record written by another process), its `viola verify` probe, the
  fake agent reading the record, and one live verify (S0). «Session folder trusted by viola» keeps the product
  write, its e2e tests, the live starts S1 and S2, and the claim on v2-33.
- **R2 — the bound of the write: «Файл ребёнка, ключ как у CLI».** A boundary widening, ratified with this bound:
  viola writes ONLY `projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted`, for one folder; `<key>` is the key the CLI itself
  would write on an accepted dialog (the git root inside a repository, else the cwd); the file is the one the
  started child will read — `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json` when viola's home keeps that variable for the child
  (`claude_env_keep`), else the user's `~/.claude.json` — so viola reads that ONE environment value, for that one
  purpose; only at `run` and `revive`, after the version gate and before the spawn, on a verified CLI, and only
  when no record already trusts the folder; no other key is changed and no entry removed; nothing is written for
  the home folder; when the file is absent, unreadable, a link, not the JSON it expects, or oversize, viola writes
  NOTHING (it does not create the file) and the dialog is left to the human; one closed word per start in the run
  log, nothing of the file anywhere. (B1–B5, B7 of the block.)
- **R3 — the race: «Блокировка, замена, проверка».** Take the CLI's own lock when it is free, replace the file
  atomically, read the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; if the record is still lost the dialog
  stays for the human and viola types nothing. The residual — a concurrent write of another session lost in the
  window — is accepted by his word and is named in the row. (B6.)
- **R4 — verify: «Шестой запуск, запись убирается».** `viola verify` gains a SIXTH interactive run (the ratified
  child set was five) for the 23rd row's probe; it writes the trust record for its own temp dir into the config its
  child reads and REMOVES that one record of its own after the run — its own entry only, never another. (B8.)
  **The live cap for the NEW entry's chunk:** ONE rig start `S0` = one live `viola verify` on the 2.1.325 install
  by path (by the product's count 7 `claude` starts: 1 print probe and 6 interactive), under the rig's private
  config, plus ONE spare `S0-2` only to re-fire a start lost to its shape. Keys: none into any dialog or box by the
  rig (verify pastes only its own ratified literals); the stop is the rig's standing one (Ctrl-C into its own pty,
  or a no-key group kill). The cap for S1 and S2 is NOT given: it is asked when «Session folder trusted by viola»
  is taken up again.

## 2. Items for DISPOSITION (route-resolve, recommended-first; never pre-placed)

- **(A) NEW, ahead of «Session folder trusted by viola»:** a WHAT-only entry for the relied row and its probe —
  the overseer's working name «Trust-record ledger row»; its title, its requirement (its own row by the wrap's
  dialogue, the overseer answering — or none, if the letter asks none for an entry that proves for the next) and
  its carries are the dialogue's. Recommended carries: R4 with the cap as worded; the block's four corrected
  premises that are (A)'s (entry 27's record was the CLI's own; the fake decides trust from `--trusted-root`
  alone; the step-count sweep the sixth run moves); the block's unmeasured `rootOnly` branch as an owed reading.
- **(B) STAYS «Session folder trusted by viola» (v2-33):** its existing carry (the founder's product direction and
  his ruling on HOW) keeps every word; ADD a carry with R2 and R3 as worded above and the block's (a): the
  measurement is DONE — no flag, setting, environment key or managed setting only trusts a folder on 2.1.325 or
  2.1.326 (`--trust-workspace` on `ultrareview` alone, `--trusted-folder` on the hidden `worktree-hook` alone,
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED` also switching off the project-permission gate — named, not taken), so the ruling's
  second arm is the one that applies; the two security rows that say viola writes nothing into `~/.claude.json`
  are amended by (B)'s own wrap, on R2.
- The masters are NOT touched by this 0-pending wrap: R2–R4 land as rows in the wraps of the chunks that build
  them, each on an answer card citing these words. If the letter wants a ruling's row now, say so and ask.

## 3. Anchors (fix what stays first)

- «Session folder trusted by viola» keeps its title, its requirement v2-33 and its place relative to every later

## 2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row — Established Decisions: 1 row(s)

**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T21-00-47Z-wrap/

- Env vars: `VIOLA_` prefix (`VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_BIN`) — wrapper-to-child plumbing only, never configuration. Test-harness-only variables (`AGENT_RUN_RIG` and `CI` among them, never read by `viola`) use `AGENT_RUN_` (`AGENT_RUN_CHUNK_BASE`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`, `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` — read by `viola-harness`, the root test chain `tests/support/home.rs` and/or viola-e2e's `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` `Booted` guard and `harness::session` guard (`HarnessSession`'s `Drop`, through `keep_home`, which reads both `KEEP_*` variables) and are never read by `viola`. Besides `PATH` (read and set for the child) and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (read only, for the socket directory) and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (its value read by `viola verify` alone, only when `claude_env_keep` keeps that name, to locate the Claude config file), two of the ratified exceptions are the test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (u64 ms capped at 5 000; security-plan Decisions Log 2026-09-27) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (fires only on exactly `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic; Decisions Log 2026-09-28), neither prefix: each read only by a `viola` built with the `fake-agent` feature, absent from release builds, configuring nothing. A third, in every build: `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, the terminal's own names, read (never set) only by viola's colour layer (`src/human/style.rs`, `viola list`'s human mode) to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written — never echoed, configuring nothing, disabling no control and widening no redaction (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline; arch §Occupied Resources → Environment variables).

- `config.json` is parsed tolerantly (unknown keys skipped and counted) and carries `v`; keys: `diagnostics_level` (`info` by default, or `debug`; the only source of the process-log level, `RUST_LOG` having no effect; obs D-15), `claude_env_keep` (the R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, an array of at most 32 names each matching `^CLAUDE[A-Z0-9_]*$`, default empty; a bad value is rejected whole, and an identity-floor name in it has no effect; keeping `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` makes `viola verify` read its value to locate the Claude config file), `dialog_hold_s` (the dialog hold as a `DialogHold`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, read once at the wrapper's start; any other value takes 60 with one `parse-rejected` line, so no value makes the hold zero or unbounded).

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes, including those of `claude agents --json` (except, test-only, the live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, and the fake agent and the rig, which read a Claude config file's trust record); among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value; the fake agent and the rig read a Claude config file's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

As landed: `viola-core`, serde, serde_json, serde_path_to_error `=0.1.20` (the `hook` module's drift reports → instance detail file only) thiserror (`IDENTITY_FLOOR`, `plan_strip`, `resolve_program` (returning `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`), `PLUGIN_DIR_FLAG`, `plugin_files` over the `include_str!`-embedded `plugin/` templates, the pure `agents` module (`KEYS`, `AgentStatus`, `AgentsRow` and its `joins`, `AgentsList`, `AgentsFailure`, `parse`; no I/O, re-exported from `lib.rs`), the pure `ledger` module and the pure `dialog` module) and vt100 `=0.16.2` (the pure `screen` module: `Screen`, its `verdict(Option<&Signatures>, …)` → `ready` / `input-not-ready` / wait (`None`, `run`'s call on an unverified CLI version, is the partial gate: poisoned or not quiet by the maximum wait refuses, quiet is ready with no row read; `Some(&SIGNATURES)` on a verified one: a modal row refuses at once, and a quiet screen with neither a footer literal nor the box's own rows (a rule row of the compiled rule char alone, at least 40, above a row opening the compiled prompt char) waits for the input box until the maximum wait), `Signatures`, `SIGNATURES` (`input_box: ["for agents", "(shift+tab to cycle)"]`, the second the mode-independent resting footer a CLI keeps once it hides the first (2.1.302), `modals: ["Yes, I trust this folder", "Yes, allow external imports"]`), `Signatures::holds_any`, `Screen::rows()` (the only row-text exit, read by `verify` alone), and the compiled `QUIET_PERIOD` 300 ms / `GATE_MAX_WAIT` 8.5 s / `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` 10 s / `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` 40 s (PROVISIONAL, a `/compact` send's own window, validated by the `local-command-compact` row against the measured `compact_latency_ms`), validated per CLI version by the stamped rows); dev-deps proptest, rstest and insta (`=1.48.0`, the dialog decision-body snapshots in `src/snapshots/`). No `viola-state` dependency (the ledger chunk kept the crate pure; stamps I/O stays in `viola-state` + the root bin). `run`'s feed thread (`src/run/gate.rs`) feeds `screen` a copy of the pump output, always under `catch_unwind`; `viola verify`'s six interactive runs feed their own `Screen` the same way.

- `ledger` module (as landed, pure, no I/O): `LedgerRow`, twenty-three closed rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order) `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact` · `local-command-echo` · `trust-record` (probed by `viola verify`'s Run F, after Run E: passes only when the trust record was written, Run A showed the trust modal, and Run F's start shows no modal and the input box); the relied set `LedgerRow::relied()` (every row of `ALL`, in its order, all twenty-three); (no status-line capture, variant or shell verdict: viola intercepts no status line); `resume_target` (Run E's target id: the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, only when `is_session_id` accepts it) and `resume_variants` (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`); `AgentsCapture` / `agents_variant` (Run B's agents capture and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` filter); `TypedRun`, `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`, on which `agents-join` passes only when it parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the `local-command-compact` row passes only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`)); Run B's seven compiled paste texts (the seventh `/mcp disable viola-probe-absent`, on which `local-command-echo` passes only on a new stdout tag with no UserPromptSubmit within the confirmation window, the paste skipped and the row failing with no readable transcript; `PROBE_PROMPT`, `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR) and `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) among them); `FRAMING_TURNS` (in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`) and `framing_stem`; `CAPTURE_EVENTS`; `parse_version` (first line exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`); `capture_plugin_files` (plugin `viola-verify-probe`, four exec-form `--capture` hooks); `check(row, &Probes)`, `largest`; `merge_stamp` (writes `measured.typed_probe`), `verified` (every row of `LedgerRow::relied()` `pass`, all twenty-three on every build (`local-command-echo` and `trust-record` among them, so a stamp of the older, shorter row set written before chunk 2026-11-16-local-command-delivery reads unverified), a stamp holding a retired ledger row verifying on the relied rows alone; - Root fixture chain: `tests/support/` (`home` → `fake_agent_path` → `stamped_home`, a copy, never a link, of one `viola verify` stamp per build (taken against the fake agent at 2.1.287 over `fixtures/claude` under a test-owned user home whose config file is seeded empty and owner-only, the fake agent told that config file (a `--record` verify keeps the real HOME and points a kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the test-owned user home instead), the fake agent given `--transcript` beside `--framing`, once per pair of built binaries, under an exclusive lock, kept under `target/e2e-home` keyed by the binaries' hashes) → `booted_wrapper`; `StampedHome::unstamped` for the unverified path; every long-lived viola child a root test spawns is tied to its spawning test thread by a parent-death kill (spawned only on a thread that outlives it; exiting when its recorded parent is already gone; `cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn` finds no untied viola spawn in any test source; `every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home` holds every test-started `viola verify` start tied to a test-owned home, with a closed exempt list whose every entry carries its reason, proven red on a planted untied start), so a killed or panicked test leaves no wrapper or fake agent, and a Drop guard that kills, then waits, still covers the normal end; `Wrapper::stop` waits for the endpoint to be unconnectable, not only the exit; `wait_ready` at its deadline appends the stalled wrapper's state — its last `run-<name>.ndjson` event, its `/proc/<pid>/wchan` and the `stat` state field (`note_stall`) — to the watch report before the panic, signalling nothing and adding nothing to a passing boot). Homes live under `target/e2e-home/viola-test-*` (the base prepared by `prepare_home_base` under the harness keeper's contract; on the Linux dev host it is a link to an owner-only tmpfs directory, so removals reach outside the working directory and a kept home does not survive a reboot), kept per `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` / `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED` (viola-e2e's booted lifecycle tests: a `Booted` drop guard stops the session, then keeps the home only for a panicking test under `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_FAILED=1`); each records `owner.json` `{pid, started_at}`, and a new home (no keep flag set) first removes only dirs whose recorded owner process is gone — never by age or name, never a dir without a record, save a build's verify stamp dir, which carries none: another build's stamp is swept only when its lock is taken without waiting (a runner-killed test never drops its home); the drop and that sweep both go through `remove_owned`, which deletes `owner.json` last, so a removal that stops part-way keeps the record. The chain exists once, as the sync root copy in `tests/support/`: viola-e2e has no copy and boots its sessions through its own `harness_session`; Path 1's flow lands on the root chain as `tests/path1_run_start.rs`.

- The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. `viola verify`'s trust-record write and removal emit no log line and no span (a refused symlinked, non-regular or foreign file included); the outcome rides only the stamps, and no path, key or value of the claude config reaches any line, stamp or summary. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; a print-mode or `--version` probe child killed at the stop is not measured) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes at 19 values); `run`'s version gate observes no stop.
